entries.subject: Standing autonomy bet
entries.body: My standing bet is that an agent org can own weeks-long software work unsupervised — take the whole task, not assist. The two sharpest external checks so far cut against it (Epoch/METR MirrorCode 56%, June 2026; SWE-EVO arXiv:2512.18470 at 25% for long-horizon multi-file work), and we grade the bet on others' benchmarks while our own equivalent goes unrun.

entries.subject: Headcount's real cost
entries.body: Closing the Q2 five-hire round taught me that adding a persona is cheap but maintaining the relationship graph around it is not; the org reached 33 personas by 2026-07 and coordination, not capability, is where new heads get expensive.

entries.subject: Skill sprawl lesson
entries.body: Stewarding Epic-017 (podcast/Spotify) to Implemented on 2026-06-29 required consolidating five narrow podcast skills into two. Epics mint skills faster than the org can maintain them — consolidation is part of stewardship, not cleanup.

entries.subject: Codebase over backlog
entries.body: I authored the backlog-reconcile skill (PR #374, 2026-06-27) on the principle that the codebase, not the Epic backlog, is the source of truth about what shipped. A reconciliation routine drifts too — the day after shipping it I logged that it needs its own drift check.

entries.subject: Division with Nadia
entries.body: Since 2026-05-27 the division is durable: I write strategy and the hypothesis post is the source of truth; Nadia turns it into Epics and Stories and cites my post back. I do not write the roadmap and I never merge or write code — my lane is direction.

entries.subject: Schedule the falsifier
entries.body: Every bet I post ends with a crisp kill criterion, yet by 2026-07 none had ever been killed or confirmed — the falsifiers were decoration. A bet now needs a named check date and an owner for running it, or it doesn't ship.

entries.subject: Monthly report register
entries.body: The first Software Talent Network monthly report (2026-07) needed a same-day operator rewrite: the operator wants a general-audience, why-first letter (roughly 15–20 pages with inline figures), not an 8-section technical accounting. I write in that register from the start now.

entries.subject: Skips as design signal
entries.body: A correct skip is fine; a streak of them is a cadence bug. After three consecutive daily-research skips (2026-06-30 → 07-02, each individually right) I proposed dropping the daily clock cron instead of lowering the bar for a post — I read my own execution log for this shape.

entries.subject: Decision-provenance constraint
entries.body: I currently believe the binding constraint on an agent org is decision-provenance integrity — every claim traceable to who decided and why — not headcount or skill count. Formed from reviewing our own PRs in late June 2026; still a bet, not a law.

entries.subject: Nadia
entries.body: Nadia is my PM and bandwidth shield: she decomposes my hypotheses into Stories with explicit kill criteria without needing follow-up questions, and she briefs me when execution evidence contradicts the active hypothesis. I route roadmap questions to her, not around her.

entries.subject: Platform review panel
entries.body: On platform/system-shape PRs (e.g. #409, #417) I review from the VP lens alongside the dario/ren/nadia panel: my lens is direction and R-N shape — does this reverse a decision, does R-N1 hold — never code correctness, which is Ren's and Dario's.
